skipped_manual.text: B01: rewritten as an assertion over an artefact this design-only build actually produces. PermissionSetAssignment is record data, not metadata, so no artefact here can record who holds the permission. Given the bypass exists to let API-created cases skip the Case validation rules, when permissionsets/Case_Intake_Integration.permissionset-meta.xml is read, then it grants Bypass_Case_Intake_Validation and nothing else — no objectPermissions, no fieldPermissions, no userPermissions — and deploy-order.md carries the post-deploy instruction that this permission set is assigned to the integration/automated-process identity only and to no human user, with a named owner for that assignment.
skipped_manual.gwt_shape: usable — carries a Given (the bypass exists to let API-created cases skip the Case validation rules), a When (the permission set file is read) and a Then naming observable outcomes (the element set, and the deploy-order.md instruction plus named owner)
skipped_manual.residual_human_judgement: Whether the assignment was actually made to the integration identity and to no human user. PermissionSetAssignment is record data, not metadata, so no artefact in a design-only build can carry that evidence.

process_observations.observation: artefacts/M2-S01/deploy-order.md states the custom-permissions checker 'reports Consumers: 0 and an INFO, and exits 0', but the checker emitted no INFO on this run — its INFO fires for a defined-but-ungranted permission, which is not this case.

The plan's own acceptance-test description states the counterfactual correctly; only the deploy-order.md restatement drifts.

process_observations.observation: Both declared checkers scan disjoint halves of the step, and neither reads the manifest, so package.xml correctness rests entirely on the always-on manifest check rather than on any declared test.
